By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No. 124/18 filed on behalf of petitioner seeking compensation under Sections 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident,
would be decided.

2. Briefly stated, the facts of the claim petition are that on 11.06.2017 at about 8:00 pm, petitioner Nilesh Kumar alongwith his friend Amandeep Singh was coming from Bhalgarh to Delhi on his motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-13SN-3027, which was being driven by Amandeep Singh at a normal speed and on correct side of the road and petitioner was pillion rider on the motorcycle.

It is further stated that when the motorcycle reached near Viswamil, Nehru Sport School, Rai, Sonipat,
Nilesh Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152148689/
1 Haryana, one Honda City car bearing registration No.HR-26AJ-1091, which was being driven by respondent No.1 / driver of the car at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from Rai Sports School and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner with a great force, as a result of which motorcycle fell down on record and petitioner sustained grievous head injuries.
It is further stated that he was immediately taken to Tulip Hospital, Sonipat, Haryana and thereafter, he was taken to Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi, where his MLC was prepared.
FIR bearing no.352/17 PS- Rai District Sonipat, was registered in connection with the accident.
3. In response to the notice of petition, all the respondents appeared and filed their replies/ written statements.

3.1 In the joint written statement filed by the respondent no.1 & 2, they stated that petition is liable to be dismissed as petitioner has not come with clean hands and has suppressed the material facts.

It is further averred that no accident was caused by respondent No.1 with vehicle No.
HR-26AJ-1091 and respondent No.1 and 2 have been falsely implicated in the accident.
It is further stated that vehicle of the respondent No.2 is insured with the respondent No.3 and respondent No.1 was having valid driving licence.

Rest of the averments of the petition are specifically denied on behalf of the respondents No. 1 & 2.
3.2
Respondent No.3 / Bajaj Allianz GIC Ltd has filed its written statement and has taken general defences.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 05.02.2020:-
(i) Whether the petitioner Nilesh Kumar suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident which happened on 11.06.2017 at about 8:00 p.m. near Vishwamil crossing and Nehru Sports School, District Sonipat, Haryana, within jurisdiction of PS Rai, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing Registration No.HR-26AJ-1091 being driven by Respondent No.1 / Anil Kumar?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of the said injury and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate of interest and for which period?

(OPP) 
(iv) Relief.
5.
In order to establish his claim, petitioner examined only one witness i.e. himself.

He deposed on the strength of affidavit Ex. PW1/A and deposed regarding manner of accident, injuries suffered by him and the medical expenses incurred on his treatment and relied upon following documents:-
 Photocopy of class Xth marksheet-cum-certificate of petitioner is  Photocopy of driving licence of petitioner is Ex.PW1/2  Photocopy of aadhar card of petitioner is Ex. PW1/3  Photocopy of ration card of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/4

Certified copy of criminal case record is Ex. PW1/5  Photocopies of treatment record and medical bills Nilesh Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152148689/
2 of petitioner are Mar X5 (colly).
Petitioner was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for respondents.
6. Respondents side opted not to lead evidence in their defence.

7. I have heard Sh. Kumar Shivam, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner ; Sh. Arun Sheoran, Ld. Counsel for R-1 and R-2 and Sh. Pranav Mishra, Ld. Counsel for R3/Insurer.
8.
The issues are decided as follows- 9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10. Now in this case, the petitioner Nilesh Kumar is injured and eye witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1.

He stated on oath in the affidavit that on 11.06.2017 at 8:00 pm, he alongwith his friend Amandeep Singh was coming from Bhalgarh to Delhi on his motor-cycle bearing registration No. DL-13SN- 3027, which was being driven by his friend Amandeep Singh at a normal speed and correct side of the road and petitioner was pillion rider on the motor-cycle.

It is further deposed by him that when he reached near Visamil, Nehru Sport School, Sonipat, Haryana, a Honda City car bearing registration No.HR-26AJ-1091, which was being driven by respondent No.1 at very high speed and in rash and negligent manner came from the side of Rai Sport School and hit the motor-cycle of the petitioner, as a result of which motorcycle fell down on road and petitioner sustained grievous injury.
PW1 was cross-examined by the respodent side at length.
During his cross-examination, petitioner stated that the road was one way and the offending vehicle was coming from the wrong side and no suggestion to the contrary was given to him.
He stated in his cross-examination that both he and driver of motorcycle were wearing helmets.
He explained the reason for about one month delay in registration of FIR by stating that delay was occassioned due to his medical condition.

Injured was only 19 years old on the date of accident and his MLC was prepared on 12.06.2017 at 12:35 am (intervening night of 11.06.2017 &
12.06.2017)
reflects alleged history of road traffic accident.
He denied the suggestion that accident had occurred due to his sole negligence.
11. After investigation, police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1/ the driver of the bus.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

sentences.text: any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
No evidence was led by any of the respondents in their defence and R1 did not enter into witness box to assail the claim of the petitioner.
13. Respondent no.1 and 2 (the driver and owner of the offending vehicle), did not lead any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner Nilesh Kumar received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1/ Anil Kumar, the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly,
this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

ISSUE No.2:
15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded Nilesh Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152148689/
4 compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

sentences.text:
17. Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to her under the afore-said heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
18.
Petitioner has placed on record only photocopies of medical bills and no original medical bills have been filed on record.
Further, perusal of duplicate inpatient Bill dated 14.06.2017, which is part of the document Mark X reflects that the amount of bills to the tune of Rs.34,464/- has been paid by the company.
Further, during oral arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner has submitted that a sum of Rs.34,464/- has already been reimbursed to the petitioner against medical expenses.
Apart from copy of this final bill, there are certain photocopies of Pharmacy bills and receipt, however, none of them are in original.
No secondary evidence has been sought to be led regarding the medical bills either at the stage of inquiry and there is no explanation for non filing of original bills.

Further,
during his cross-examination, PW1 / petitioner admitted that all his treatment expenses were paid by his father and later on, the same was reimbursed to his father by the insurance company i.e.
United India Insurance Company Ltd against health insurance policy.
No one from the hospital was summoned to prove the final bill.
Under this head, only original medical bills are to be considered.
Hence, no amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
19.

According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was taken to Tulip Hospital, Sonipat,
Haryana, where first aid was given to him and thereafter, he was taken to Max Hospital, Patparganj,
Delhi on the same day of accident where his MLC No. 6672/17 was prepared and he remained admitted there till 14.06.2017.
Perusal of copy of discharge slip and other annexed documents of discharge summary reflects that the petitioner suffered undisplaced fracture in the left frontoparietal convexity.
There is no other document which suggest hospitalization of the petitioner after 14.06.2017.
Further, charge-sheet also suggest that the petitioner received grievous injuries in the accident.

In his examination in chief, petitioner has deposed that he took medical treatment as an outdoor patient for a period of six months, however, he has not placed on record a single medical treatment paper / document / prescription after 14.06.2017.
However, it cannot be ignored that petitioner suffered head injuries and he must have been in a bad condition after the accident and remained on bed for a considerable period of time.
He must have endured immense pain and difficulty in his day to day life.
In these circumstances, considering the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20.
In his examination in chief, PW1 / petitioner has claimed that he had spent a sum of Rs.20,000/- on his conveyance and Rs.20,000/- on special diet.

However, he has not proved any actual expenses in relation to conveyance and only photocopy of one ambulance bill of Rs. 3000/-
(which is part of Mark X) is placed on record.

Except this only bill, there is no other document of Nilesh Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152148689/
5 conveyance.

entities.text: Nilesh Kumar vs Anil Kumar on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, I deem it fit to grant Rs.20,000/- to petitioner for conveyance.

Though no document has been placed on record by the petitioner to suggest that he has spent a sum of Rs.20,000/- on special diet, still considering the nature of injuries and hospitalization of the petitioner, it can be assumed that that petitioner might have needed a special diet for recovery.
Thus, I deem it fit to grant a sum of Rs.20,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet.
21. During his examination-in-chief, PW1 deposed that he had spent a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant charges, however, no evidence was led in this regard.

Though no cogent evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment, it cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner might have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- as attendant charges.

22. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.55,000/- (20,000+20,000 + 15,000)
under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :-
23.

In his examination in chief Ex. PW1/A, petitioner deposed that he was working as a Technical Sales Executive with "Good Karma Information Technology", Sector-8, Noida, U.P. and was getting a salary of Rs. 13,000/- per month +incentive.
However, no documentary evidence has been led by the petitioner to substantiate his plea.
During his cross-examination, he averred that he has not placed on record his payslips or any bank statement to show that he was receiving a salary of Rs.13,000/- +incentive.
Further, no witness has been called / summoned from "Good Karma Information Technology, Noida, U.P. to prove his income.
He has also proved on record his academic document i.e. class X mark sheet cum certificate Ex. PW1/1 showing that he is a matriculate.
Aadhar card of the petitioner Ex. PW1/3 shows that he is the resident of Delhi but petitioner himself disclosed address of his employer as that of Noida, U.P..
He nowhere averred that he was working or was gainfully employed in Delhi.

In view of the above-said discussion, in my considered view, the income of the petitioner has to be taken as per the minimum wages applicable to skilled worker prevalent in Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident as his place of employment is that of Noida, U.P., and the same is Rs.9118/- per month.
Thus, the income of the petitioner is considered to be Rs.9118/- per month.

As discussed above, it can be fairly assumed that the petitioner would not have been able to continue daily affairs in usual manner and must have remained incapacitated to work for about 5 months, even though no leave record is filed or proved on record.
His income is assumed be Rs.9118/- per month.
Hence, on account of loss of income, an amount of Rs.45,590/- (9118X5) is being awarded as compensation under this head.

24. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

 ISSUE NO. 3 (INTEREST):
25.
Petitioner has pursued his case since the year 2018.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5%
per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
26. Thus, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

LIABILITY:
27.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.3/ insurer shall be entitled to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
28.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.1,51,000/- (rupees one lakh and fifty one thousand only) along with interest @
7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3/ insurer.

This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
29.
With these observations, the present claim petition is disposed off.
30. File be consigned to Record Room.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.1,51,000/- (rupees one lakh and fifty one thousand only) along with interest @
7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3/ insurer.

This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
29.
With these observations, the present claim petition is disposed off.
